title: Retracement to Order Block with Screener
summary: Marks an order block in three steps: a range-breaking momentum candle, a close beyond it, and the retracement back to its level, with a table of recent entries.
descriptionHtml:
The study looks for an order block in three numbered steps. Signal 1 is a momentum candle: its body is more than 66 percent of its range, its range is at least one 14-bar ATR (average true range), and it breaks the range of the previous Period candles. A bearish candle that makes a new low below the lowest low marks a long setup; a bullish candle that makes a new high above the highest high marks a short setup. Only the first such candle after the side changes counts.

Signal 2 is a later candle of the opposite colour that closes beyond the first candle: above its high for a long, below its low for a short, again with a range of at least one ATR. Signal 3 is the entry: after signal 2, price crosses back into the order block level, which is the first candle's high for a long or its low for a short. Vertical Offset pushes that level out by a share of the first candle's range, so price need not touch it exactly.

Each step is marked with a small numbered circle, below the candle for a long and above it for a short. A line is drawn from the newest first candle at its high or low and extended to the right, and a table lists the most recent third signals with their time, side and close.
howToReadHtml:
Read the numbers as a sequence. A 1 shows a strong candle that swept the recent range, a 2 shows price closing back through that candle, and a 3 shows price returning to the level the first candle left behind, which is where the setup expects an entry. A 3 never appears without a 1 and a 2 before it on the same side: each step waits for the step before it.

The extended line keeps the newest order block level on screen, and the table gives a quick list of the latest entries. The signals use only closed bars and fixed rules, so they say nothing about the size of the move that follows; a level that price cuts straight through is not a defended level.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: How many earlier candles the first candle must break the high or low of. A longer period asks for a larger sweep and gives fewer setups.

settings.label: Vertical Offset (%)
settings.html: Pushes the order block level out by this share of the first candle's range, so the third signal fires a little before an exact touch. 0 needs a precise touch.

settings.label: Direction
settings.html: Which sides the table lists: both, only long entries or only short entries. The markers are not affected.

settings.label: Only Bullish
settings.html: When off, long entries are left out of the table.

settings.label: Only Bearish
settings.html: When off, short entries are left out of the table.

settings.label: Display Rows
settings.html: How many of the most recent third signals the table lists. 0 leaves only the header.

settings.label: Table Position
settings.html: Where the table sits. Tables pin to a corner, so a centre column is drawn on the right and a middle row at the bottom.

settings.label: Table Size
settings.html: Kept for the text size of the table; the table is drawn at the chart's own text size in this version.

settings.label: Style
settings.html: Style of the order block line: solid, dashed or dotted.

settings.label: Width
settings.html: Thickness of the order block line, from 1 to 10.

faq.q: Why can signal 2 never appear on the same candle as signal 1?
faq.html: Signal 2 must be a candle of the opposite colour to the first candle, closing beyond it, and the first candle cannot close beyond its own high or low. It always lands on a later candle.

faq.q: What does the Vertical Offset do?
faq.html: It moves the order block level away from the first candle by a share of that candle's range: above its high for a long, below its low for a short. At 50 the level sits half the candle's range beyond the extreme, so a shallower pullback is enough for signal 3.

faq.q: Why is there only one line on the chart?
faq.html: The line always shows the newest first candle's level. When a new first candle appears, the old line is removed and a new one is drawn from the new candle.

faq.q: Which time zone does the table use?
faq.html: The table writes each signal's time in the chart's own timezone, as hour and minute plus the date on an intraday chart, and the date alone on a daily one.

deviation: The table is drawn at the chart's own text size whatever Table Size says, and a middle row or centre column is drawn in the nearest corner, because a table here has no size setting and pins only to a corner.

related.title: Mitigation Block Scanner
related.summary: Finds the nine-pivot swing pattern of a mitigation block on a zig zag and marks the bar where the close breaks through it, or the later retest of that level.
